analysis: The closest option retains the eight-course legal/gateway/transnational-law sequence with accounting, finance, economic incentives, organisational behaviour, negotiation and business strategy. It replaces product prototyping and general market research with AI/economic governance and public economics, strengthening corporate institutions and regulation. Actual corporate-law doctrine, shareholder remedies and Dutch tax/procedure remain explicit gaps.

The corporate-responsibility option retains substantial legal study and replaces geology, farming, an unspecified partner project and generic data methods with economic foundations, public economics, accounting and public-policy analysis. Climate science, environmental governance, justice and communication then provide specific complementary substance for environmental responsibility rather than substitutes for environmental liability law. Six advanced courses are present; the policy substitution materially implements regulatory decision-making rather than being an unrelated quota fix.

Every selected contribution was reconsidered from its available profile or description. Corrected inherited rationales naming courses from a different curriculum and false claims that transnational transactions teach Dutch company formation, rhetoric supplies legal procedure, or negotiation supplies moot-court doctrine. Description-only public-policy analysis is used within its actual policy-framework and memo scope. The second option is qualitatively distinct and exceeds thirty credits each way; innovative-company strategy remains covered by the closest option without a manufactured third programme.

Four original offering conflicts are resolved through current-term rescheduling and substantively motivated changes. Every formal prerequisite is earlier; law/business/statistical and economic foundations precede their dependants. Two twenty-four-course schedules have four courses per term, first-year PPD and at least six advanced courses. No planning value is restored.

Thirteen partial relationships were reassessed from actual content: broad private law matches the broad introduction, criminal liability matches substantive liability, transnational arbitration matches legal-dispute practice, and negotiation matches only the ADR part of civil procedure. Accounting/corporate finance is a strong identifiable financial-method relationship. Organisational psychology is partial to organisation/strategy, and general ethics partial to business ethics. Seventeen dedicated legal components retain meaningful gaps; business foundations are not company-formation law, and economics is not tax-law doctrine. Optional research is outside scheduled credits.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, literature evaluation, civic collaboration and reflective practice provide the first-year common foundation.

BENBUSI112.name: Accounting & Corporate Finance
BENBUSI112.contribution: develops financial statements, accounting, organisational control, accountability and discounted-cash-flow appraisal, providing actual financial analysis for enterprise decisions

BENBUSI211.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
BENBUSI211.contribution: examines AI, firms, regulation, corporate responsibility, labour and inequality through business and country research, providing an institutional perspective on innovative-company governance

BENBUSI311.name: Transnational Business Law
BENBUSI311.contribution: examines legal frameworks for cross-border contracts, trade, finance, intellectual property and digital commerce, with advisory assignments and simulated arbitration

BENBUSI312.name: Money, Banking & Finance
BENBUSI312.contribution: examines financial instruments, valuation, banks, risk, regulation and monetary institutions, with bank simulation and evidence-based financial decisions; it complements corporate financing rather than teaching company-law doctrine

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.contribution: introduces economic choice, markets, strategic interaction and government’s economic role as specific foundations for analysing regulation

BENECON311.name: Public Economics
BENECON311.contribution: examines public goods, taxation, spending, externalities and redistribution through policy models and research; this is an economic contribution rather than tax-law doctrine

BENENTR211.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
BENENTR211.contribution: examines marketing strategy, consumer psychology, responsible brands and primary/secondary evidence in business decisions; this is a complementary account of firm strategy, not legal consumer-protection training

BENENTR312.name: International Business & Governance
BENENTR312.contribution: examines trade, institutions, policy conflict and cross-border business decisions, supporting the international commercial context of legal practice

BENGATE101.name: Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations
BENGATE101.contribution: develops business models and the functions of enterprises, providing organisational context and the formal foundation for transnational business law without claiming company-law doctrine

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: develops empirical design, measurement, statistics and a data-collection project as a methodological complement to socio-legal inquiry

BENLEAD112.name: Leadership Communication
BENLEAD112.contribution: examines leadership communication, culture, persuasion and ethics through interviews, advisory work and speeches, complementing organisational responsibility and professional communication

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.contribution: examines motivation, leadership, teams, power, conflict and organisational change, including evidence synthesis for organisational cases

BENLEAD312.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
BENLEAD312.contribution: develops bargaining, interests, power, trust and strategic conflict management through negotiation simulations and scenario design

ENSDELT312.name: Governance of Sustainability
ENSDELT312.contribution: examines institutions, power, participation, justice and collective decisions in sustainability, with stakeholder consultation and policy advice/evaluation

ENSGATE101.name: Sustainability Essentials I
ENSGATE101.contribution: introduces planetary boundaries and scientific methods for understanding environmental pressures and sustainability interventions

ENSSUST111.name: Climate Change
ENSSUST111.contribution: examines climate science, impacts, adaptation, mitigation, justice and governance, supplying scientific and social substance for environmental regulation

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.contribution: introduces legal traditions, public/private law, justice and social context through case briefs, legal interpretation, mock trials and a socio-legal proposal

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
GOSLAWJ111.contribution: examines human-rights law, protection institutions, landmark cases and philosophical justifications through legal and normative argument

GOSLAWJ211.name: Criminal Law & Criminal Justice
GOSLAWJ211.contribution: examines criminal liability, punishment, criminalisation, excuses, offences and participation, with legal-advice memoranda and a criminology research proposal

GOSLAWJ212.name: Introduction to Public International Law
GOSLAWJ212.contribution: examines international legal sources, state responsibility, institutions, force, human rights and treaty politics through legal cases and critical research

GOSLAWJ213.name: Comparative Constitutional Law
GOSLAWJ213.contribution: compares constitutional structures, rights, courts and judicial review, with administrative participation, remedies and procedural fairness

GOSLAWJ311.name: Principles of Private Law
GOSLAWJ311.contribution: examines property, tort and contract rights across legal systems through legal briefs, comparative contract research and simulated mediation

GOSLAWJ312.name: Foundations of European Union Law
GOSLAWJ312.contribution: examines EU institutions, competences, legal effect, remedies, citizenship and free movement through current judgments and legal cases

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: develops ethical interpretation, normative argument and independent positions on moral theory and practical questions relevant to legal judgement

GOSPOLI312.name: Public Policy Analysis
GOSPOLI312.contribution: examines policy-making processes and alternative analytical frameworks through a sugar-policy case and policy memos, supporting the legal-governance perspective

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: examines social institutions, inequality, identity and boundaries through social theory and evidence, complementing analysis of law’s social context

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: develops qualitative design, interviews, documentary inquiry, coding and interpretation for empirical investigation of social and institutional questions

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.contribution: examines environmental-justice movements, collective action and feminist/anticolonial perspectives through actual environmental cases

MCCCOMM111.name: The Art of Rhetorical Communication
MCCCOMM111.contribution: develops rhetorical analysis, argument construction, debating and public speaking; its communication contribution is distinguished from legal procedure

MCCCOMM212.name: Communicating the Climate Crisis
MCCCOMM212.contribution: examines climate communication, public argument and contested policy through media analysis and an intervention in public debate

MCCMEDI212.name: Media & the Environment
MCCMEDI212.contribution: examines representations of ecological risk, scientific knowledge and human–environment relations as forces in public debate and environmental ethics

alignment.rationale: Both develop financial analysis and investment valuation relevant to enterprise financing. UCR combines accounting and discounted-cash-flow appraisal; Tilburg applies valuation specifically to corporate-law questions.

Both develop legal-source analysis, written legal advice and oral advocacy in a simulated business dispute. UCR uses transnational arbitration; Tilburg uses company-law courtroom pleadings and Dutch procedure.

Both examine market behaviour, incentives and strategic interaction as analytical foundations. Tilburg explicitly applies economics to legal rules, transaction costs, property and corporate-law decisions.

Both examine organisations, structure, motivation and organisational decisions. UCR emphasises psychological and group dynamics; Tilburg combines organisation theory and business strategy for company-law students.
Both study methods for resolving disputes. UCR develops negotiation and bargaining through simulations; the relationship concerns dispute resolution and does not reproduce Dutch civil procedure.
Both develop legal concepts, source interpretation, case analysis and legal reasoning in social context.
Both develop substantive human-rights law and its philosophical and institutional foundations. Tilburg concentrates on the Dutch and European legal setting.
Both examine criminal acts, causation, intent, guilt, justifications, excuses and participation as grounds and limits of criminal liability.
Both provide public-international-law study. UCR applies legal sources and principles to contemporary cases and treaty politics; this is a partial subject relationship.
Both examine state organisation, rights and constitutional constraints. UCR uses comparison and includes administrative principles; Tilburg establishes Dutch constitutional foundations.
Both develop property, contract and tort concepts through legal cases. UCR compares legal systems while Tilburg establishes the Dutch private-law foundations.
Both examine the EU legal order, national effects, citizenship, free movement and remedies. Tilburg additionally addresses competition law and procurement.
Both develop normative analysis of responsibility and competing obligations. UCR provides ethical theory and argument; Tilburg applies ethics specifically to enterprise.
No selected course centres European legal history.
